proposals.before: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang Chi to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
proposals.after: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang hurrying to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 第二息章馳到京都: 章 is the son's name and 馳到 means "hurried/galloped to"; "Zhang Chi" wrongly treats 馳 as part of the name.

proposals.before: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang Chi to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
proposals.after: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang hurrying to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 章馳到 as a personal name Zhang Chi.

proposals.before: In the time of Emperor Wu of Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an county.
proposals.after: In the time of Emperor Wu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an county.
proposals.reason: After Xu Zhicai's arrival in Luoyang under Northern Wei, 武帝時 refers to the northern Emperor Wu (Xiaowu), not Liang Emperor Wu; the literal English already omits "of Liang".

proposals.before: Before long he was relieved of attendant-in-ordinary and enfeoffed as marquis of Chiyang county.
proposals.after: Before long he was appointed palace attendant and enfeoffed as earl of Chiyang county.
proposals.reason: 除侍中 means appointment to 侍中, not relief from office; 伯 is earl/count, not marquis.

proposals.before: Soon he was removed as Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chiyang county.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Earl of Chiyang county.
proposals.reason: Same errors: 除 is appoint; 伯 is not marquis.

proposals.before: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Chao, and the like were not within the amnesty.
proposals.after: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Cha, and the like were not within the amnesty.
proposals.reason: 賊詧 is Xiao Cha (詧); "Chao" is the wrong reading of the name.

decisions.reason: In s0025, 第二息章馳到京都 names the second son 章 and uses 馳到 as the verb of travel; reading 章馳 as the personal name Zhang Chi invents a two-character name and drops the hurrying sense.
The same Chinese parses as son 章 plus 馳到京都; the literal's Zhang Chi wrongly absorbs 馳 into the name, and the proposed Zhang hurrying to restores both name and verb.
s0087's bare 武帝時 sits after Xu Zhicai's Northern Wei Luoyang career and before Eastern Wei 天平; adding of Liang misidentifies the emperor as Liang Wudi rather than the northern Emperor Wu.
尋除侍中 is appointment to 侍中, not relief from office, and 池陽縣伯 is an earldom (伯), not a marquisate (侯); the proposed wording corrects both errors.

decisions.after: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Earl of Chiyang county.
decisions.reason: 除侍中 and 池陽縣伯 do require appointment and earl, but Attendant-in-Ordinary is this chapter's rendering of 散騎常侍 (s0089), not 侍中; Palace Attendant matches the Chinese office.
賊詧 is the rebel named 詧 (Xiao Cha); Chao is the wrong reading of 詧, and Cha restores the attested personal name.
